chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, who said:
I saw Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام praying while blood was flowing from his shanks.

Because this report is to be understood as referring to that from which it is difficult to guard oneself, such as persistent wounds and boils with which precaution is not possible; and that is indicated by this.

key_terms.سَاقَيْهِ: his two shanks or lower legs
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ: interpreted or understood in a particular legal sense
key_terms.ٱلدَّمَامِيلِ: boils or sores producing blood or discharge
key_terms.ٱلدَّمُ: blood present on the body during salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلِاحْتِرَازُ: guarding oneself against or avoiding something

ai.seo_question: Does blood from ongoing wounds invalidate salat (prayer) when it is difficult to avoid?
ai.summary: This report describes Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام praying while blood flowed from his legs, and it is understood as applying to cases where avoiding blood is extremely difficult. The significance of the report in fiqh is that ongoing wounds or boils may be treated as excused situations regarding ritual purity in salat (prayer).
